Mulki left me with salt in my hair, bruises on my knees, and memories I’ll be holding onto for a long time.

Went there to learn surfing, came back learning how to fall, laugh, and try again. Met new people, shared the best kind of chaos with my closest friends, and lived a few days that felt bigger than they should’ve been. Sore, sunburnt, and completely happy. I’d do it all again.

Most people talk about grief like it’s a problem to solve. Either you outrun it, or you collapse under it. As if those are the only endings available.
But sometimes it’s neither.
Sometimes it’s quieter than that. It sits beside you at breakfast. It walks with you to work. It shows up in small pauses and familiar songs. It doesn’t disappear, and it doesn’t have to.
Living with grief isn’t dramatic. It’s ordinary. It’s learning the shape of it, making space for it, and still choosing to move forward. Not because it hurts less — but because life keeps asking you to participate.
There’s a strange strength in that. Not defeating it. Not denying it. Just carrying it gently, and continuing anyway.
Our experiences define our love and our love defines our experiences

Embrace your muse. When rain whispers against your window, write about it. Call it a dance of droplets, nature’s gentle song. If it calms your spirit, it’s meaningful. 

You’re tuned into the world’s quiet beauty; be proud of that. Noticing small wonders, you create a tapestry of gratitude that makes the world warmer. Shadows on a loved one’s face, the hush before dawn, if these moments stir you, hold them dear. They remind you that joy is woven into existence. 

Celebrate seeing the universe in a grain of sand, feeling eternity in a moment. This pursuit of beauty, this joy in simple things, it’s precious. Nurture it, for it brings you to life.

From Nietzsche’s “Thus Spoke Zarathustra,” 

“Like the solitary peaks that stand tall and undaunted, let your spirit rise above the mists of conformity. In the symphony of existence, be not just another note that fades into the echoes of the multitude, but a distinct melody that sings the truth of your unique essence. The society around you is but a canvas; your will and capabilities, the brush and colors with which you paint your destiny. Forge your path with the fire of your own potential, for in the vast landscape of life, it is the self-crafted journey that leads to the most majestic of vistas.”

MEANING:

Think of yourself as a tall mountain, standing strong by yourself. Don’t just follow what everyone else is doing. Instead, be special and true to who you are. Society is like a background, and you have the power to create your own story on it. Use your own skills and decisions to shape your life. Just like a mountain makes its own way through the sky, you should make your own path in life. When you do things your own way, you’ll reach amazing places.
